title: The Critical Patch Size Problem in Random Graphs
summary: The problem of {\it critical patch size} -- a threshold condition for population persistence -- is investigated in the context of discrete habitats, modeled as graphs with a distinguished subset of vertices acting as sinks. These sinks impose boundary-like constraints analogous to Dirichlet conditions in continuous domains. The population proliferates locally at the vertices and diffuse across the network through the graph Laplacian. In the sinks the population cannot survive.
